*See also: [Modbus Client](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client#configuration-variables)*

read_coils.docs: Reads one or more coils (function code `0x01`).

count.docs:
**templatable**: 1-2000 discrete inputs to read. Defaults to `1`.

*See also: [Modbus Client](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client#configuration-variables)*

read_discrete_inputs.docs: Reads one or more discrete inputs (function code `0x02`).

read_holding_registers.docs: Reads one or more holding registers (function code `0x03`).

read_input_registers.docs: Reads one or more input registers (function code `0x04`).

read_address.docs:
**templatable**: Address of the first holding register to read back.

*See also: [Modbus Client](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client#configuration-variables)*

read_count.docs:
**templatable**: 1-125 registers to read back. Defaults to `1`.

*See also: [Modbus Client](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client#configuration-variables)*

values.docs:
**templatable**: Registers to **write**, `write_address` first. 1-121 registers - the `0x17` write ceiling, lower than the 123 of a plain write. As a lambda it must return a `std::vector<uint16_t>`.

*See also: [Modbus Client](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client#configuration-variables)*

write_address.docs:
**templatable**: Address of the first holding register to write.

*See also: [Modbus Client](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client#configuration-variables)*

read_write_multiple_registers.docs: Writes one block of holding registers and reads another back in a single transaction (function code `0x17`). Per the Modbus specification the write is performed **before** the read, so when the two ranges overlap the read returns the values just written. Because the write travels in the same frame, an `on_no_response` retry re-sends it - avoid retries on registers whose writes have side effects (command or trigger registers, counters, one-shot commits). For queue priority and duplicate suppression the hub classifies `0x17` as a write, so a second identical send while one is in flight is refused with `on_not_sent` rather than requeued the way a plain read would be.

on_response.docs:
**[Automation](https://esphome.io/automations/)**: Fires on a standard-conforming reply. The lambda variable it carries depends on the action - see below.

*See also: [Modbus Client](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client#configuration-variables)*

pdu.docs:
**templatable**: The PDU to send: function code followed by data. The device address and CRC are added automatically - do **not** include them. Maximum 253 bytes (the Modbus PDU limit): an empty or over-long YAML list fails config validation. As a lambda it must return a `modbus::helpers::PduBuffer` (a fixed-capacity stack vector, not `std::vector`): `return {0x03, 0x00, 0x10, 0x00, 0x01};` works, and so does directly returning the result of a `modbus::helpers::create_*_pdu()` builder - see [Building PDUs with Helpers](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client#building-pdus-with-helpers). Unlike the YAML list, a lambda result isn't length-checked: one over 253 bytes is silently truncated to the limit rather than rejected. An empty lambda result (or a builder that fails - see below) also produces an empty PDU; the hub refuses to send it, and `on_not_sent` fires.

*See also: [Modbus Client](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client#configuration-variables)*

address.docs:
**templatable**: The Modbus device address the frame is sent to. Accepts `0`-`255`; the valid Modbus device range is `1`-`247`, and `0` is broadcast (no reply will ever arrive; see [Behavior](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client#behavior)).

*See also: [Modbus Client](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client#configuration-variables)*

on_sent.docs:
**[Automation](https://esphome.io/automations/)**: Fires when the frame is written to the wire. Lambda variable: `request` (`std::span<const uint8_t>`, the PDU sent).

*See also: [Modbus Client](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client#configuration-variables)*

on_error.docs:
**[Automation](https://esphome.io/automations/)**: Fires on a Modbus exception response. Lambda variables: `request` (`std::span<const uint8_t>`) and `exception_code` (`modbus::ExceptionCode`, an enum - cast to `int`/`uint8_t` to print).

*See also: [Modbus Client](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client#configuration-variables)*

on_no_response.docs:
Fires when the device does not answer within the hub's `send_wait_time`. Same three forms as `modbus_client.send`'s `on_no_response` above: a returning lambda, a `then:` automation, or a `then:` automation with a nested `retry:` returning lambda.

*See also: [Modbus Client](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client#configuration-variables)*

on_not_sent.docs:
**[Automation](https://esphome.io/automations/)**: Fires when the frame never reached the wire - a duplicate write already pending, a full send queue, an invalid request, or a queued frame cancelled by another device or automation clearing the queue for the same address. See [Behavior](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client#behavior). Lambda variable: `request` (`std::span<const uint8_t>`, the PDU that was not sent).

*See also: [Modbus Client](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client#configuration-variables)*

send.docs: This action queues a custom Modbus frame for transmission and optionally handles the outcome.

values.docs:
**templatable**: Coils to write, `start_address` first. 1-1968 coils. As a lambda it must return a `std::vector<bool>`.

*See also: [Modbus Client](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client#configuration-variables)*

write_multiple_coils.docs: Writes one or more consecutive coils (function code `0x0F`).

values.docs:
**templatable**: Registers to write, `start_address` first. 1-123 registers. As a lambda it must return a `std::vector<uint16_t>`.

*See also: [Modbus Client](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client#configuration-variables)*

write_multiple_registers.docs: Writes one or more consecutive holding registers (function code `0x10`).

write_single_register.docs: Writes a single holding register (function code `0x06`).

address.docs:
**int**: The Modbus device address every call from this client targets. Unlike [Modbus Controller](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_controller/), there is no default.

*See also: [Modbus Client](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client#configuration-variables)*

id.docs:
**[ID](https://esphome.io/guides/configuration-types#id)**: The ID to use in lambdas. Unlike most components it is not generated for you: the device is only reachable through `id()`, so an entry without one is rejected.

*See also: [Modbus Client](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client#configuration-variables)*

modbus_id.docs:
**[ID](https://esphome.io/guides/configuration-types#id)**: The Modbus hub to send on. Automatically assigned when a single hub is configured.

*See also: [Modbus Client](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client#configuration-variables)*

address.docs:
**templatable**: The device address the frame is sent to. Accepts `0`-`255`; the valid Modbus device range is `1`-`247`, and `0` is broadcast (no reply will ever arrive; see [Behavior](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client#behavior)).

*See also: [Modbus Client](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client#configuration-variables)*

modbus_id.docs:
**[ID](https://esphome.io/guides/configuration-types#id)**: The Modbus hub to send on. Automatically assigned when a single hub is configured.

*See also: [Modbus Client](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client#configuration-variables)*

on_error.docs:
**[Automation](https://esphome.io/automations/)**: Fires on a Modbus exception response. Lambda variables: `request` (`std::span<const uint8_t>`, the request PDU this action sent - same as in `on_response`) and `exception_code` (`modbus::ExceptionCode`, an enum - cast to `int`/`uint8_t` to print). There is no `response` span, as an exception carries no data payload.

*See also: [Modbus Client](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client#configuration-variables)*

on_no_response.docs:
Fires when the device does not answer within the hub's `send_wait_time`. `request` (`std::span<const uint8_t>`, the PDU that got no reply) is available in every form. Three ways to write it:

*See also: [Modbus Client](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client#configuration-variables)*

on_not_sent.docs:
**[Automation](https://esphome.io/automations/)**: Fires when the frame never reached the wire - for example, an empty PDU, a duplicate write already pending (see [Duplicate suppression](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client#behavior)), a full send queue, or cancelled by another device or automation clearing the queue for the same address. Distinct from a timeout: nothing was transmitted. Lambda variable: `request` (`std::span<const uint8_t>`, the PDU that was not sent).

*See also: [Modbus Client](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client#configuration-variables)*

on_sent.docs:
**[Automation](https://esphome.io/automations/)**: Fires when the frame is written to the wire. Lambda variable: `request` (`std::span<const uint8_t>`, the PDU sent). This fires once per transmission, before any reply, and does not fire when the send ends in `on_not_sent` (nothing was transmitted). Exactly one of `on_response`/`on_error`/`on_no_response`/`on_not_sent` follows each transmission attempt - a retry reopens this cycle for its own attempt; see [Behavior](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client#behavior).

*See also: [Modbus Client](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client#configuration-variables)*

count.docs:
**templatable**: 1-125 registers to read. Defaults to `1`.

*See also: [Modbus Client](https://esphome.io/components/modbus_client#configuration-variables)*
